claims.statement: Let D contain normalized generating laws supported on the complete-data fiber compatible with the observed event, and let P_theta be the normalized complete-data model. Minimize D_KL(Q||P_theta) over the pair. A generalized forward step reduces it in Q at fixed theta; a generalized backward step reduces it in theta at the updated Q. Exact forward minimization over the unrestricted desired family gives the current conditional posterior, and exact backward minimization maximizes expected complete-data log likelihood. A constrained family changes the optimization problem. Finite, continuous KL on the relevant domain is an explicit premise here.

evidence.locator: Sections2.1-2.2, pp2052-2054 / PDF4-6; Eq4 and Figure2

claims.statement: The inspected convergence theorem requires compact parameter space, an eventually entered compact invariant generating-distribution set, a closed update map, continuous finite objective, nonincrease, and strict decrease outside the set of joint coordinatewise global minimizers. It concludes objective convergence and membership of accumulation points in that set, not necessarily convergence of the whole parameter sequence. For the unrestricted desired family, additional interior differentiability conditions give stationary observed-likelihood accumulation points; stationary does not mean a local maximum. Separate coordinate descent tests need extra hypotheses, such as the unique forward minimizer in Proposition5, to establish the composite equality condition.

evidence.locator: Section3 Definition1, Theorems2-3, Corollary4 and Proposition5, pp2058-2062 / PDF10-14; AppendicesA-B, PDF20-24

claims.statement: D_KL(Q||P_theta)=D_KL(Q||P_theta(.|observed))-log p_theta(observed). Decreasing the paired divergence may lower observed likelihood when the posterior approximation gap also changes. The paper’s constrained two-coin example moves theta from0.3 to0.4, reducing likelihood from0.58 to0.52 and reaching a restricted fixed point that is not likelihood-stationary. Even exact EM can stay at the likelihood minimum theta=0.5 in that example.

claims.statement: Positive common support alone does not ensure finite KL on an arbitrary countably infinite state space. Continuous-observation extensions also need suitable measures and regularity. The incremental-EM argument applies to the inspected finite cyclic full sweep with unique admissible cached M minimizers and the theorem’s compactness/closedness hypotheses, not every random or unfair schedule. The displayed Section4 GEM comparison has its Q inequality reversed; it is not adopted as an ascent rule.

claims.statement: Choose a normalized tractable family q_lambda(z) on latent states compatible with observed x and a model p_theta(x,z). At fixed theta optimize F(lambda,theta)=E_q[log p_theta(x,z)-log q_lambda(z)], equivalently minimize KL(q_lambda||p_theta(z|x)). Then, holding q fixed, maximize its expected complete-data log likelihood over theta and repeat. Exact coordinate optima give the source’s restricted projection formulation; checked partial ascent steps give a generalized realization. The latent family, model support and finite expectations must be specified.

The lower bound equals log p_theta(x)-KL(q_lambda||p_theta(z|x)). Bound ascent therefore does not generally imply observed-likelihood ascent or exact posterior recovery. At a differentiable interior fixed pair with a stationary parameter M-step, the observed log-likelihood gradient equals the theta gradient of that KL gap with q fixed. A zero gap is sufficient for the usual touching-bound argument, but zero gradient of the gap can also occur when the gap is positive; stationary error is not necessarily a local error minimum.

evidence.locator: Section3 decomposition, p2060 / PDF12; Section5 stationary-error discussion, pp2065-2067 / PDF17-19

claims.statement: The source’s broad claim that an independence approximation permits likelihood stationarity only in an exact-family degenerate case is not adopted as a general impossibility theorem. In the saved normalized counterexample, p_theta(y,z)=Bernoulli_theta(y)*r(z), fixed correlated r has probabilities(0.3,0.2,0.2,0.3), and the unique best product approximation is uniform. Its positive KL gap is independent of theta, so variational EM still attains the observed-data likelihood optimum. This qualifies the general prose without refuting the conditional GAM theorem.

evidence.locator: Section5 broad independence-approximation argument, pp2066-2067 / PDF18-19; curator finite counterexample

claims.statement: A mean-field fixed-point equation alone does not establish the global restricted E minimizer. The GAM convergence assumptions, including compactness, continuity, closed maps and sufficient strict progress, remain necessary for the cited conditional result. The printed fixed-q Boltzmann KL derivative has the opposite sign: the correct derivative is model moment minus q moment, although setting either sign to zero gives the same moment equation. Marginal independence of one pair does not alone imply a zero direct interaction when other latent paths can cancel its marginal association.

aio_mappings.rationale: The method constructs and selects clusters from unlabeled points. The inspected target denotes an unsupervised clustering process/task; this related match preserves the algorithm-versus-task distinction without asserting equivalence or an upstream subclass.

claims.statement: For each center y and beta>0, assign original points weights P_y,beta(x)=exp(-beta*||x-y||^2)/sum_u exp(-beta*||u-y||^2). Iterate y_new=sum_x x*P_y,beta(x) at fixed beta. Start centers at observations at a sufficiently high initial beta, retain their point memberships, track converged centers, and combine memberships when centers coalesce. Decrease beta and warm-start the retained centers; the printed schedule divides beta by1.05 and uses200inner iterations in demonstrations. The weighting set remains the original observations, not an unweighted replacement by merged centers.

evidence.locator: Section2 Eq2.1-2.5, pp90-91 / PDF2-3; Section3 Eq3.1 and Melting Procedure, pp92-94 / PDF4-6

claims.statement: For nominal cluster Q at its tracked center, fractional free energy M_Q(beta)=sum_(x in Q)P_y,beta(x) is a membership weight fraction. Choose a threshold M_T; a cluster is good where its fraction exceeds that threshold, and robustness is the corresponding range of logarithmic scales. Greedily select the most robust good cluster, remove its ancestors and descendants from consideration, and repeat. Observations not covered by selected clusters remain in a leftover set; complete coverage is hoped for in the source, not guaranteed. Threshold choice and tie handling affect the result.

evidence.locator: Section4 Eq4.1, Definition2 and Melting Algorithm steps1-6, pp95-98 / PDF7-10

claims.statement: Stationary centers satisfy the weighted-mean equation for F=-log Z/beta, but not every fixed point is a local minimum or exponentially attracting. For points{-1,+1}, the update is tanh(2*beta*y): at beta=1, y=0 stays at an unstable free-energy maximum if initialized exactly there; at beta=0.5, the critical map tanh(y) has derivative one and no uniform local geometric rate. The one-dimensional bifurcation condition2*beta*weighted_variance=1 does not establish higher-dimensional global cluster recovery.

claims.statement: The printed merge step says more than two coincident clusters, while the surrounding prose describes two-cluster mergers; this record uses the intended two-or-more interpretation explicitly. Exact coincidence tolerance, robust tie policy and a universally adequate initial scale are not specified. Finite inner iteration does not certify convergence or finite exact tree completion. native_neighbors.definition: A hierarchical model for collections of discrete observations in which each document draws a Dirichlet-distributed mixture over a fixed finite set of topics, and each token draws a topic and then an observation from that topic’s categorical distribution.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: The defining feature is a shared prior over document-specific topic proportions together with repeated per-token topic selection. This differs from PLSA’s fitted document-index weights and a mixture selecting one topic for a whole document. The model is distinct from its variational EM, sampling or other inference algorithms. The bare LDA alias is omitted because AIMech already uses it for the unrelated Gaussian classifier LinearDiscriminantAnalysis. limitations: The number of topics is finite and fixed in this construction. Integrating a continuous Dirichlet mixture does not introduce infinitely many topic classes. Infinite exchangeability supports the representation discussed in Section 3.1; arbitrary finite exchangeability alone is not the asserted theorem.

Given observed topic assignments, Dirichlet conjugacy is exact. With topics unobserved, the marginal posterior over proportions is generally not a single Dirichlet; gamma=alpha+expected counts is a variational update, not exact marginal conjugacy. Exact inference is generally difficult, and bound optimization need not monotonically improve the true likelihood or attain its global maximum.

The basic model ignores word order and explicit within-topic dependencies, though integrating document proportions induces dependence between tokens. Zero word probabilities require smoothing or other support handling for novel documents. A prior over document mixtures does not guarantee freedom from overfitting, identifiable topics or meaningful semantic labels.

The Bayesian topic-prior extension requires expected log topic probabilities in its assignment update. The appendix’s printed alpha Hessian has a sign/factor mismatch with the preceding gradient; the consistent Hessian is M*(trigamma(sum alpha)-delta_ij*trigamma(alpha_i)). This record does not adopt that printed Hessian as verified code. Equation (13) correctly uses the normalized posterior.

The comparison’s empirical mixture over training-document indices must weight an entire document once; the printed p(d) inside its token product is not adopted. These mathematical qualifications do not establish an error in unseen author software or experiments.

The source’s document, classification and recommendation experiments have distinct protocols. No exact likelihood replication, generic performance advantage or biological-mechanism conclusion is claimed. All source material concerns the specified 2003 model, not every later topic-model extension.

claims.statement: For a fixed K, positive alpha_i and normalized topic-word probability rows B_i, draw theta_d~Dirichlet(alpha) independently for each document. Given a document length N_d, draw z_dn~Categorical(theta_d) and w_dn~Categorical(B_zdn) for each token. Conditional on theta_d and B, token probabilities are sum_i theta_di*B_iw and tokens are independent; integrating theta_d gives p(w_d|alpha,B)=integral Dir(theta_d;alpha)*product_n(sum_i theta_di*B_i,w_dn)dtheta_d. claims.statement: For fixed K topics beta_k on a finite vocabulary, draw document logits eta_d from N(mu,Sigma), set theta_d=softmax(eta_d), then independently draw each topic assignment z_dn from theta_d and its word from beta_zdn, conditional on these variables. The logistic-normal prior allows associations that a single Dirichlet proportion prior cannot express, including positive pairwise proportion covariance when at least three components are available. Dirichlet proportions are not literally independent: their sum-to-one constraint gives negative off-diagonal covariance for positive concentration parameters. Common shifts of all logits leave proportions unchanged; unrestricted K-logit mean/covariance parameters are not uniquely identified by the induced composition. Logit covariance, proportion covariance and causal relationships are distinct.
